predecessors.name: Emirate of Afghanistan
predecessors.text: Dost Mohammad's Kabul and Ghazni: 'the British marched to Kabul with no resistance from Dost Mohammad's troops'; 'in August 1839, after thirty years, Shuja was again enthroned in Kabul'

predecessors.name: Principality of Kandahar
predecessors.text: Kandahar: 'Fall of Kandahar: 8 May 1839'; the page lists '1839: Durrani Empire (Shah Shuja)' as the principality's successor

successors.name: Emirate of Afghanistan
successors.text: Kabul and Ghazni: Dost Mohammad's restoration in April 1843 ('Restoration: April 1843', Emirate infobox)

successors.name: Principality of Kandahar
successors.text: Kandahar: 'Liberation of Kandahar: 9 August 1842'; 'They occupied Kandahar and re-established the principality.'

ledger.x: August 1839: Shuja Shah is enthroned at Kabul by the British.
October 1842: the Army of Retribution leaves.
April 1843: the British-backed Durrani restoration ends and Dost Mohammad resumes at Kabul.

wars.name: First Anglo-Afghan War
wars.outcome: Barakzai victory (infobox): the British enthroned Shuja in August 1839, lost the Kabul uprising of 2 November 1841 and the retreat of January 1842, retook Kabul in September 1842 and withdrew in October; Dost Mohammad returned in April 1843.

certainty.note: The state held what the British garrisoned (Kabul, Ghazni and Jalalabad, with Kandahar until 9 August 1842); no frontier line is described, and the Sikh frontier at Peshawar and the Khyber is approximate.
